title: Setting Up Node.js Environment
description: Understanding how to install and configure the Node.js environment.

quiz.question: Which website is the official source to download Node.js?
quiz.explanation: The official Node.js downloads are available at https://nodejs.org.

quiz.question: Which package manager comes bundled with Node.js by default?
quiz.explanation: npm (Node Package Manager) is bundled with Node.js by default.

quiz.question: Which command initializes a new Node.js project with a package.json file?
quiz.explanation: `npm init` creates a new package.json file for your project.

quiz.question: How can you check the installed version of npm?
quiz.explanation: `npm -v` or `npm --version` will display the npm version.

quiz.question: Which file is used to specify the metadata and dependencies of a Node.js project?
quiz.explanation: package.json contains project metadata and dependency info.

quiz.question: Where are the installed Node.js packages stored by default?
quiz.explanation: Installed packages are stored in the node_modules directory.

quiz.question: Which command installs all dependencies listed in package.json?
quiz.explanation: `npm install` installs all dependencies from package.json.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the .nvm (Node Version Manager)?
options: To manage multiple versions of Node.js
quiz.correctAnswer: To manage multiple versions of Node.js
quiz.explanation: nvm helps switch between different Node.js versions easily.

quiz.question: Which command runs a Node.js file named app.js?
quiz.explanation: `node app.js` executes the JavaScript file using Node.js.

quiz.question: Which environment variable commonly defines the port number for a Node.js server?
quiz.explanation: The PORT environment variable is widely used to specify the server's port.
